text: A part such as a motor or gripper that turns the controller's decisions into physical motion.
The small play in a gear train that lets the output move slightly without the input moving, which robot reducers keep to about an arc-minute or less.
A system that guides the cable carrier to prevent cable loops in the robot work area.
The central component in ros2_control that manages controller lifecycles and connects them to hardware-abstraction interfaces to run the main control loop.
An industrial Ethernet ring topology featuring an active ring supervisor transmitting beacon frames, achieving a worst-case recovery time of 2890 µs on copper with default beacon settings.
A camera setup in which the camera is mounted on the robot's gripper and moves with it.
An MTC stage that creates robot states on its own, such as the current state or a set of candidate grasp poses, without needing a neighboring stage's result.
Time-critical connected communications in EtherNet/IP that transport I/O data using UDP without embedded protocol headers.
A condition where an integrator accumulates excessive error while the actuator is saturated, causing severe overshoot and delay upon desaturation.
Lithium polymer rechargeable battery common in mobile robots for its high energy density; Battery University gives about 3.6 V nominal per cell, and hobby packs are often labeled slightly higher.
A ros2_control stand-in for a real robot that simply copies each command into its state, so software can be tested with no robot or physics.
A joint move, in which all joints move together to reach a target, so the tool usually does not travel in a straight line; it is written MoveJ in ABB RAPID.
Controlling a machine tool's motion with numbers stored on a medium, developed for machine tools in the 1950s and a bridge between punched cards and robot programs.
Open Navigation LLC, the company that provides leadership, maintenance, development and support services for Nav2.
A set of data points in 3D Cartesian coordinates representing physical external surfaces sampled by depth sensors.
A readable, high-level programming language widely used in robotics for scripting, testing and higher-level logic, and one of the two main languages used with ROS.
Maintenance done after equipment has failed or stopped.
The ROS document that names the coordinate frames mobile robots use, such as map, odom and base_link.
The official bridge suite that translates messages between Gazebo multi-physics simulation transport and ROS 2 publish-subscribe topics.
A two-way communication pattern in ROS where a client node sends a request to a server node and waits for a response, used for quick one-off tasks.
Simultaneous Localization and Mapping, the method a mobile robot uses to build a map of an unknown room while tracking its own location inside it.
A robot wrist whose last three joint axes meet at one point, which lets inverse kinematics split into a position part and an orientation part.
Teleoperation software that captures user input from a keyboard, joystick, or gamepad and publishes motion velocity commands.

The working point of the tool, such as the tip of a welding wire or the center between gripper fingers, which the robot positions and moves; on ABB robots the default tool0 has its TCP at the mounting flange.
A motion plan in which an axis speeds up at constant acceleration, cruises at its maximum speed, then slows down at the same rate, so its speed-time graph is a trapezoid.
The Python-like text scripting language that executes on Universal Robots controllers for motion, I/O, and real-time threads.
Windows Subsystem for Linux version 2, a Windows tool that runs a real Linux kernel, allowing developers to install Ubuntu and run ROS tools directly on Windows.
How robot programs are organized (RAPID modules and routines, URScript functions and threads) and how they recover from errors such as a missed pick, with a 3 by 3 palletizing loop.
The full math of a planar two-link arm: forward kinematics, the reachable ring, closed-form inverse kinematics with atan2, rounding edge cases, and the Jacobian singularity.

Build a ROS 2 camera pipeline in Python: sensor_msgs/Image and CameraInfo, optical frames, image_transport, cv_bridge conversion, and real-time OpenCV edge processing; runs without a camera using cam2image test images.

Capstone project: an open-source ROS 2 cell monitor that reads robot state, packed Modbus handshake bits and a camera check from stand-in servers, keeps a maintenance log, and ends with a real pull request. No hardware needed.
